Imam Ahmad said:

"Whoever recites (sāla sā'il) says: it means 'a valley flowed' (sāla wād).

And whoever recites (sa'ala sā'il) says: it means 'he called out' (da'ā)."

I (Ibn al-Qayyim) say: This is one of the two opinions.

The second is that this alif also comes from al-su'āl (asking), but the hamza in it has been changed into an alif.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 70, verse 16:

Imam Ahmad said:

"It devours the flesh of the calves of the legs."

I say: There are two well-known interpretations of the verse.

The first is that al-shawa (the extremities) are the parts of the body that are not vital, such as the hands and the feet, which it strips away from their places.

From this comes the saying of the Arabs, "He shot the game and shawahu (wounded its extremities)," meaning that he struck its extremities without striking its vital spots. If he struck the vital spot and it died on the spot, it is said, "He shot it and asmahu (killed it outright)." But if the arrow pierced it and it fled with it and then died in another place, it is said, "He shot it and anhahu (brought it down after a flight)."

A poet said:

"So he does not bring down a shot (target) ... it has no count among its kind."

The second interpretation: al-shawa is the plural of shawah, which is the skin of the head and its scalp.

Ahmad's interpretation does not contradict this, so perhaps he mentioned the flesh of the calves only as an example, and Allah knows best.

The second: the word has been altered from its usual pattern for the sake of rhyme (izdiwāj) with khāli', and it has a parallel.

As for the semantic matter: stinginess and cowardice are the two most corrupt qualities in a servant, especially when his stinginess is hali', meaning it has caused him to be anxious in his anxiety, and his cowardice is khāli', meaning his heart has been dislodged from its place, so there is neither generosity, nor courage, nor benefit from his wealth or his body. As one says "lā ṭaʿnatun wa lā jafnatun" (neither a spear-thrust nor a platter), and "lā yuṭrad wa lā yushrad" (he is neither driven away nor does he drive away). If you wish to know the halū', he is the one who, when hunger afflicts him, for example, shows complaint (istijāʿa) and hastens to it; when pain afflicts him, he hastens to complain and displays it; when subjugation afflicts him, he shows submission and humiliation and returns with it quickly; when hunger afflicts him, he quickly throws himself down on his side and shows complaint; when an opportunity for greed appears to him, he flies to it quickly; and when he attains it, he places it in his soul in the place of the spirit, so there is no forbearance and no generosity.

All of this comes from the smallness and baseness of the soul, its concealment in the body, its hiding, and its debasement. And Allah is the One sought for help.

[Section: The difference between tenderness of heart and jaza']

The difference between tenderness of the heart (riqqat al-qalb) and jaza' is that jaza' is weakness in the soul and fear in the heart, nourished by intense greed and longing, and it arises from weakness of faith in qadar (divine decree). Otherwise, whenever one knows that what is decreed will certainly occur, jaza' becomes pure toil and a second calamity. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿No calamity befalls upon the earth or within yourselves except that it is in a Book before We bring it into being. Indeed, that is easy for Allah. (22) So that you will not grieve over what has escaped you or exult over what He has given you.﴾

Whenever the servant believes in qadar and knows that calamity is decreed in the present and the absent, he does not experience jaza' nor exult.

This does not negate tenderness of heart, for it arises from the attribute of mercy, which is a perfection, and Allah, glory be to Him, only shows mercy to His merciful servants.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most tender-hearted of people and the furthest from jaza'. So tenderness of heart is compassion and mercy, while his jaza' is sickness and weakness. Jaza' is the state of a heart sick with the world, which has been covered by the smoke of the commanding self (al-nafs al-ammāra), so it seizes its breath and constricts its paths to the Hereafter, and it becomes in the prison of desire and the self, a prison of narrow sides and dark paths. Thus the heart is confined and constricted, and it is anxious over the slightest thing that befalls it and cannot bear it.

When the light of faith and certainty in the promise shines in it, and it is filled with love and reverence for Allah, it softens, and compassion and mercy come to dwell in it. Then you see him merciful, tender-hearted toward every relative and Muslim, showing mercy to an ant in its hole and a bird in its nest, let alone his own kind.

This is among the hearts nearest to Allah.

Anas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most merciful of people toward dependents.

When Allah wills to show mercy to a servant, He settles in his heart compassion and mercy. And when He wills to punish him, He removes mercy and compassion from his heart and replaces them with harshness and hardness.

In the authentic hadith: "Mercy is only removed from the wretched."

And in it: "He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy."

And in it: "Show mercy to those on earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you."

And in it: "The people of Paradise are three: a ruler who is just and charitable; a man who is merciful and tender-hearted toward every relative and Muslim; and a chaste person who abstains, having dependents."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, surpassed the Ummah only by the general mercy that was in his heart, in addition to his siddiqiyya (truthfulness). For this reason its effect appeared in all his positions, even regarding the captives at Badr; and the matter settled upon what he advised, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cited as examples Jesus and Abraham. The Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, is al-Ra'uf al-Rahim (the Most Kind, the Most Merciful), and those nearest to Him among creation are the greatest in kindness and mercy, just as those farthest from Him are those who possess the opposite of His attributes. This is a gate that only the exceptional few in the world enter.

For this reason its effect appeared in all his positions, even regarding the captives at Badr; and the matter settled upon what he advised, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cited as examples Jesus and Abraham. The Lord, glory be to Him and exalted, is al-Ra'uf al-Rahim (the Most Kind, the Most Merciful), and those nearest to Him among creation are the greatest in kindness and mercy, just as those farthest from Him are those who possess the opposite of His attributes. This is a gate that only the exceptional few in the world enter.

Stillness in prayer is the constancy about which Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who are constant in their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 23].

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Ibn Lahiʿa: Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me that Abu al-Khayr informed him, saying: We asked ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir about the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Those who are constant in their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 23]. "Are they those who pray continually?" He said: "No, but when one of them prays, he does not turn to his right or to his left, nor behind him."

I say: These are two matters. The first is persistence in it (al-dawam ʿalayha), and the second is being constant in it (al-mudawama ʿalayha). So this is al-dawam, and al-mudawama is in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who are watchful over their prayers﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 34].

Al-dawam has been explained as stillness of the limbs and tranquillity (al-tuma'nina).

Al-Hasan said: "Two sounds are cursed: the flute at a melody, and the wailing at a calamity."

Abu Bakr al-Hudhali said: "I said to al-Hasan: Did the women of the Emigrants (muhajirat) do what the women do today?

He said: No. But here there is the scratching of faces, the tearing of collars, the plucking of hair, the slapping of cheeks, and the flutes of Satan. Two ugly and shameful sounds: at a melody if it occurs, and at a calamity if it befalls. Allah mentioned the believers, saying:

And you have made in your wealth a known right for the singing girl at a melody, and the wailing woman at a calamity."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 70, verse 33:

God has forbidden the Fire to whoever bears witness that there is no god but God with the true reality of the testimony (haqiqat al-shahada). It is impossible that whoever has realized the true reality of this testimony and stood by it should enter the Fire, as the Exalted said: ﴿And those who are steadfast in their testimonies﴾.

So he is one who stands by his testimony outwardly and inwardly, in his heart and his body. Among people, there are those whose testimony is dead, and those whose testimony is asleep, so that when it is roused it wakes up, and those whose testimony is lying down, and those whose testimony is closer to standing. It stands in the heart in the position of the spirit in the body. So there is a spirit that is dead, a spirit that is sick and close to death, a spirit that is closer to life, and a spirit that is healthy and standing by the welfare of the body.

In the sound hadith from him (ﷺ): "I know a word that no servant says at the time of death except that his spirit finds rest (rawh) in it." So the life of this spirit is by the life of this word within it. Just as the life of the body is by the presence of the spirit in it, and just as whoever dies upon this word is in Paradise, enjoying it, so whoever lives by realizing it and standing by it, his spirit moves freely in the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-ma'wa), and his life is the finest of lives. He said: ﴿But as for one who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the self from desire, then indeed the Garden will be the refuge﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 40-41].

So the Garden is his refuge on the Day of Meeting.

And the Garden of knowledge (ma'rifa), love, intimacy with God, longing for His meeting, joy in Him and contentment with Him, and it is the refuge of his spirit in this abode. Whoever has this Garden as his refuge here, the Garden of Eternity will be his refuge on the Day of the Promise. And whoever is deprived of this Garden is far more deprived of that Garden.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 70, verses 38–39:

And if you reflect on the connection between one of the two sentences and the other, you will find beneath it a great treasure of the treasures of knowledge and learning. By the beginning of His creation from what they know, namely the drop of semen and what follows it, He (glorified is He) pointed to the place of proof and the sign that indicates His existence, His oneness, His perfection, and His singularity in lordship and divinity. It also indicates that it is not fitting for Him, along with that, to leave them neglected, without sending to them a messenger or sending down to them a book. And it indicates that He is not incapable, along with that, of creating them anew after He has caused them to die, and of resurrecting them to an abode in which He will repay them for their deeds, good and evil.

"So how can they hope to enter Paradise while they deny Me, deny My messengers, and set up equals to My creation, when they know from what thing I created them?"

This is similar to His saying: ﴿Have We not created you? Why then do you not believe?﴾ Yet they used to believe that He was their Creator; but He argued against them by His creating them, as evidence for His oneness, His knowledge, and the truthfulness of His messengers. So He called them, from among themselves and from His creation, to affirm His names and attributes, His oneness, the truthfulness of His messengers, and belief in the Return.

**Benefit: al-mashriq and al-maghrib between the plural, the dual, and the singular**

Among this same meaning is the occurrence of al-mashriq (the east) and al-maghrib (the west) in the Qur'an, sometimes in the plural, sometimes in the dual, and sometimes in the singular, each placement being suited to what its context requires.

The first, the plural, is like His saying: ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾

The second, the dual, is like His saying: ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

The third, the singular, is like His saying: ﴿Lord of the east and the west; there is no god but Him, so take Him as your Trustee (wakil)﴾

Reflect on the profound wisdom in the variation of these passages in singular, plural and dual according to their contexts, which will reveal to you the greatness and majesty of the Noble Qur'an, and that it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy. Wherever it is in the plural, the intended meaning is the easts and wests of the sun throughout the days of the year, and these are many. Wherever it is in the singular, the intended meaning is the two horizons of east and west. Wherever it is in the dual, the intended meaning is the eastern and western points of its rising and setting, for it begins by rising until it reaches the furthest limit of its height and elevation; this is its eastern point of ascent, and from it arise the autumn and winter seasons.

So the whole of its eastern point of ascent is made one east, and the whole of its eastern point of descent is made one east, and their two wests correspond to them. This is the reason for the variation of these in singular, dual and plural.

As for the reason each passage is specific to what occurs in it, I have not seen anyone address it or open its door, and it is, praise be to God, clear from the context.

Then Ibn al-Qayyim said:

Then consider their occurrence in the plural in Surat al-Ma'arij, in His saying: ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that We are able to replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone.﴾

Since this oath is in the context of the vastness of His lordship and the comprehensiveness of His power, and what is sworn to concerns their lords and the bringing of better than them, He mentioned the easts and wests, because they include the movement of the sun, which is one of His great and mighty signs, and His moving it and turning it each day between an east and a west.

So whoever does this, how could He be unable to replace these people and bring in better than them in their place?

Also, the effect of the easts and wests of the sun on the differing conditions of plants and animals is well known. God, in His wisdom, made this a cause for the transformation of plant bodies and the changing states of animals, and their passing from one state to another. He replaces heat with cold and cold with heat, summer with winter and winter with summer, along with all the other transformations and changes of the states of animals and plants, the winds, rains and snows, and other transformations and changes occurring in the world because of the differing easts and wests of the sun. That is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.

So how could He not be able, with what they witness of this, to replace them with better?

He emphasised this meaning with His saying ﴿and We are not to be outdone﴾, and so only the plural form suits this place.

He said in (al-Tibyan):

Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that We are able to replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone.﴾

He swore by the Lord of the easts and the wests, and these are either the easts and wests of the stars or the easts and wests of the sun. Since every direction has an east and a west, He used the plural in one place, the singular in another, and the dual in another. He said ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾. It was said that they are the eastern points of summer and winter. Each place has what suits it. In Surat al-Rahman comes ﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾, because it is a surah in which pairs are mentioned: creation and teaching, the sun and the moon, the stars and the trees, the heaven and the earth, the grain and the fruit, the jinn and mankind, the material of the father of mankind and the father of the jinn, the two seas, Paradise and the Fire, and the division of Paradise into two high gardens and two lower ones, and He informed that in each garden there are two springs. So it was entirely fitting to mention the two easts and the two wests.

As for Surat Sa'ala Sa'il, He swore by the generality of His power and its perfection and the soundness of its connection to their being returned after non-existence. He mentioned the easts and wests in the plural, since that is more indicative of what is sworn to, whether the intended meaning is the easts and wests of the stars, or the easts and wests of the sun, or every part of the two directions of east and west. All of that is a sign and proof of His power, Most High, to replace the likes of these deniers and bring them into being in what they do not know, bringing them into another mode of existence, just as He brings the sun each day from a rising point and takes it away at a setting.

As for Surat al-Muzzammil, He mentioned the east and the west in the singular, because the intended purpose was the mention of His lordship and His oneness. Just as He alone is Lord of the east and the west, so He should be singled out for lordship, for reliance upon Him alone. There is no lord of the east and the west other than Him, so likewise no god and no trustee other than Him should be taken. Similarly Moses said to Pharaoh when he asked him ﴿And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ and he said ﴿The Lord of the east and the west and what is between them, if you would use your reason.﴾ In His lordship over the easts and wests is an indication of His lordship over the heavens and what they contain: the sun, the moon and the stars; His lordship over what lies between the two directions; and His lordship over the night and the day and what they comprise.

Then He said ﴿We are able to replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone.﴾

That is, We are able to take them away and bring in those more obedient to Us and better than them, as He, Most High, said ﴿If He wills, He will take you away, O people, and bring others; and God is ever capable of that.﴾ His saying ﴿and We are not to be outdone﴾ means that this will not escape Me if I want it, nor will it be beyond Me. He expressed this meaning by His saying ﴿and We are not to be outdone﴾, because the one who is overcome is outpaced by the victor in what he wants, so it escapes him. For this reason it is construed with (ʿalā, "upon") rather than (ilā, "to"), as in His saying ﴿and We are not to be outdone upon replacing your likes﴾.

For when it embeds the meaning of being overcome and subdued, it is construed with (ʿalā), unlike when it is "outpaced to it", for there is a difference between "sabaqtuhu ilayhi" (I outpaced him to it) and "sabaqtuhu ʿalayhi" (I outpaced him in respect of it). The former means "you overcame him and subdued him in it", and the latter means "you arrived at it before him".

(Section)

The reporting of His power over replacing them has occurred, in some places, with replacement by better than them; in some, with replacement by their likes; and in some, with His substituting other people who will not be their likes. These are three matters whose similarities and differences must be known. Wherever replacement by better than them occurs, it is a report of His power to take them away and bring one more obedient and more pious to Him than them in this world. That is His saying ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be like you﴾, meaning, rather, they will be better than you. Mujahid said: He replaces them with whomever He wills of His servants, making them better than these. But they did not turn away, praise be to God, so He did not replace them.

As for His mention of the replacement of their likes, it is in Surat al-Waqi'ah and Surat al-Insan. In al-Waqi'ah He said ﴿We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone upon replacing your likes and bringing you into being in what you do not know.﴾

And in Surat al-Insan He said ﴿We created them and strengthened their frames, and when We will, We can replace their likes with a complete replacement.﴾

Many exegetes said the meaning is: when We want to create a creation other than you, no one will outpace Us, and that will not escape Us.

As for His saying ﴿And when We will, We can replace their likes with a complete replacement﴾, it means: when We will, We destroy them and bring their counterparts, making them a replacement for them.

Al-Mahdawi said: people agreeing with them in creation but differing from them in action. Al-Wahidi and Ibn al-Jawzi did not mention any view other than this. On this view, these verses are a parallel to His saying ﴿If He wills, He will take you away, O people, and bring others﴾, so it is an argument from His power to remove them and bring their likes, to His bringing them back themselves when they die.

Then, Most High, He argued from the first creation, reminding them of it, saying ﴿And you have certainly known the first creation, so why do you not remember?﴾ He alerted them, by what they knew and witnessed, to the truth of what His messengers told them of the second creation.

What I hold regarding the meaning of these two verses, the verse of al-Waqi'ah and that of al-Insan, is that the intended meaning of replacing their likes is the new creation and the afterlife they were promised.

Al-Zamakhshari was successful in understanding this from Surat al-Insan, when he said: "And We replaced their likes in the severity of their binding", meaning the other creation.

He then said: "It was said: and We replaced others who would obey, and it should have been introduced with (in, "if") not (idha, "when"), like His saying ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people﴾."

I say: His use of (idha), which is used only for what is certain to occur, indicates that this replacement is certainly realised and will occur without doubt, and that is the other creation, whose possibility He argued from by His saying ﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾.

He argued from the like to the like, and against what they denied by what they had witnessed and seen. Their being their likes is their being brought into a new creation of the same kind: they are themselves, in their very persons, and they are their likes; they themselves will be returned.

So if you say "the resurrection is this same first one," you are right; and if you say "it is its like," you are right. It is the same returned, or it is a like of the first. God Most High clarified this by His saying ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation﴾.

This new creation is what includes their being their likes, and God, Glorified and Exalted, has named it a return (i'adah); and the return is like the origin; He named it another mode of existence, which is like the first; and He named it a new creation, which is like the first creation, as He said ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation? Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation﴾.

He named them likes, and they are themselves; so the words of the Qur'an agree and some of them confirm others and explain others.

With this, the difficulties raised by those who did not understand the return reported by the messengers from God are dispelled. Nor do they understand from this statement what some later scholars said, that they are others entirely in every respect.

That is certainly an error; God forbid that anyone should believe it. Rather, they are their likes and they are themselves. When you understand the realities, no one will quibble over wording except the narrow-minded, small-intellected and weak in knowledge.

(Section)

When He had established the proof against them and cut off their excuse, He said ﴿So leave them to plunge and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾

This is a severe threat, containing the abandonment of these people, against whom My proof was established, yet they did not accept it, did not fear My might, and did not believe My messages, in their plunging into falsehood and their play. Plunging into falsehood is the opposite of speaking the truth, and play is the opposite of striving that benefits its striver. The first is the opposite of beneficial knowledge, and the second the opposite of righteous action. So they neither speak the truth nor act rightly. This is the condition of everyone who turns away from what the Messenger brought; he must have both of these.

(Note: the passage is translated as given.)

What I hold regarding the meaning of these two verses, the verse of al-Waqi'ah and that of al-Insan, is that the intended meaning of replacing their likes is the new creation and the afterlife they were promised.

Al-Zamakhshari was successful in understanding this from Surat al-Insan, when he said: "And We replaced their likes in the severity of their binding", meaning the other creation.

He then said: "It was said: and We replaced others who would obey, and it should have been introduced with (in, "if") not (idha, "when"), like His saying ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people﴾."

I say: His use of (idha), which is used only for what is certain to occur, indicates that this replacement is certainly realised and will occur without doubt, and that is the other creation, whose possibility He argued from by His saying ﴿And you have certainly known the first creation﴾.

He argued from the like to the like, and against what they denied by what they had witnessed and seen. Their being their likes is their being brought into a new creation of the same kind: they are themselves, in their very persons, and they are their likes; they themselves will be returned.

So if you say "the resurrection is this same first one," you are right; and if you say "it is its like," you are right. It is the same returned, or it is a like of the first. God Most High clarified this by His saying ﴿Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation﴾.

This new creation is what includes their being their likes, and God, Glorified and Exalted, has named it a return (i'adah); and the return is like the origin; He named it another mode of existence, which is like the first; and He named it a new creation, which is like the first creation, as He said ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation? Rather, they are in doubt about a new creation﴾.

He named them likes, and they are themselves; so the words of the Qur'an agree and some of them confirm others and explain others.

With this, the difficulties raised by those who did not understand the return reported by the messengers from God are dispelled. Nor do they understand from this statement what some later scholars said, that they are others entirely in every respect.

That is certainly an error; God forbid that anyone should believe it. Rather, they are their likes and they are themselves. When you understand the realities, no one will quibble over wording except the narrow-minded, small-intellected and weak in knowledge.

(Section)

When He had established the proof against them and cut off their excuse, He said ﴿So leave them to plunge and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾

This is a severe threat, containing the abandonment of these people, against whom My proof was established, yet they did not accept it, did not fear My might, and did not believe My messages, in their plunging into falsehood and their play. Plunging into falsehood is the opposite of speaking the truth, and play is the opposite of striving that benefits its striver. The first is the opposite of beneficial knowledge, and the second the opposite of righteous action. So they neither speak the truth nor act rightly. This is the condition of everyone who turns away from what the Messenger brought; he must have both of these.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 70, verse 43:

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Toward a goal, or a sign they race toward."

This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Al-Hasan said: "It means toward their idols (ansab), which of them will touch them first."

Al-Zajjaj said: "This is according to the reading of those who read nusub with two dammas, like His words: ﴿And what was slaughtered on the altars (al-nusub)﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3]."

He said: "Its meaning is: idols for them."

The point is that a nusub is anything set up, whether a piece of wood, a stone, or a sign.

And al-iyfad (ifada, hurrying) means hastening.

And he said in (al-Tibyan):

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned their state when they come out of the graves, saying: ﴿On the Day they emerge from the graves in haste, as if they were rushing to a target they are set up to reach (nusub), hastening﴾

That is, they hasten. The nusub is the sign, the goal set up and aimed at.

This is one of the most subtle, clear and fine comparisons, for people rise from their graves hurrying toward the caller, heading toward the voice, not swerving from it to the right or left, as He said: ﴿On that Day they will follow the caller, with no crookedness in it﴾.

That is, they accept from every direction toward his voice and his side, without deviating from it.

Al-Farra said: This is like when you say: "I called you a call with no crookedness in it for you."

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that there is no crookedness for them in responding to his call, that is, they are able only to follow it and head toward it.

If you say: if the meaning is "no crookedness for them in my call," how does He say "no crookedness in it"?

It is said: one group holds that the lam is in the sense of ʿan, meaning "no crookedness away from it."

Another group holds that the meaning is "no crookedness for them away from My call," as al-Zajjaj said.

Both opinions involve an evident strain. Since the call reaches everyone without deviating from any of them, and all of them head toward the caller's voice and follow it without swerving from it, the use of the lam brings together both meanings and indicates them both.

The meaning is: there is no crookedness in His call, neither in making them hear it nor in their answering it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 70, verse 44:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Their eyes downcast, humiliation covering them.﴾

So He described them with the humiliation of the outward (ẓāhir) and the humiliation of the inward (bāṭin). The humiliation of the outward is the downcast of their eyes, and the humiliation of the inward is what covers them of abasement, from which their eyes are downcast. Close to this is His saying: ﴿And faces that Day will be gloomy, expecting that some calamity will be done to them.﴾

Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿And humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah. It is as if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night.﴾

The opposite of this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, it is granted to you that you will not be hungry therein nor be unclothed.﴾

So He negated from him hunger, which is the humiliation of the inward, and nakedness, which is the humiliation of the outward.

Its opposite also is His saying: ﴿And He will give them radiance and joy.﴾ So radiance (naḍra) is the honour of the outward and its beauty, and joy (surūr) is the honour of the inward and its beauty.

Similar to this also is His saying: ﴿Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink.﴾

So He combined for them the adornment of the outward and the inward.

Similar to this is His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to conceal your private parts and as adornment; but the clothing of righteousness – that is best.﴾

So He combined for them the adornment of the outward and the inward.

Similar to this is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with stars and as protection from every rebellious devil.﴾

So He adorned its outward with the stars and its inward with protection from every accursed devil.

Similar to this is His saying also: ﴿And He formed you and perfected your forms and provided you with good things.﴾

Close to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the best provision is piety.﴾

And from it is His saying: ﴿As for those whose faces turn black, [it will be said], "Did you disbelieve after your belief? Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny." But as for those whose faces turn white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide eternally.﴾

So for those He combined the beauty of the outward and the inward, and for those (the others) He combined the blackening of the outward and the inward.

And from it is the saying of the wife of the ruler: ﴿That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I had sought to seduce him, but he refused.﴾

So she described his outward with beauty and his inward with chastity; she thus described him with the beauty of the outward and the inward, as if she said: this is his outward, and his inward is better than his outward.

All of this indicates to you the connection of the outward with the inward, in decree and in law. And Allah knows best what is correct.
